content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Elvis Operator** as part of **Null Safety and Type Handling**. The Elvis operator `?:` evaluates its right-hand expression only when the left expression is null, making defaults and early returns concise. Use the subtopics—Using ?:, Supplying Default Values, Early Returns with the Elvis Operator—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The Elvis operator `?:` evaluates its right-hand expression only when the left expression is null, making defaults and early returns concise.

items.title: Early Returns with the Elvis Operator
items.text: Early Returns with the Elvis Operator is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.

content_blocks.code:
fun displayName(input: String?): String = input ?: "Guest"

fun main() = println(displayName(null))
